data.narrative:
Arbe Robotics is a public-stage company in the Drones & Autonomous sector that has raised $118M to date. The valuation universe for this company is constrained: while seven private peers operate in Drones & Autonomous—including Joby Aviation, Archer Aviation, Zipline, Nuro, and Elroy Air—there are zero public comparables in this narrow sector. This structural limitation significantly constrains traditional peer-based valuation methodology.

The Peer-Median method is not applicable to Arbe. The analysis identified only two same-stage peers within Drones & Autonomous, zero adjacent-stage peers, and zero similar-tier comparables. Since a meaningful peer-median triangulation requires at least three datapoints within the filtered set, the five total same-sector peers cannot support a reliable median multiple without introducing material selection bias. Expanding to an all-sector median would dilute sector-specific dynamics and is accordingly rejected.

Given the failure of peer-median triangulation, alternative methods (DCF, precedent transaction, venture-capital method) would be required to establish a defensible valuation range. The primary uncertainty is the absence of public market pricing signals for robotics-stage autonomous companies, leaving analyst estimates exposed to discount-rate and terminal-value assumptions. Without additional methodological results or market data, no quantitative valuation range can be responsibly stated at this stage.
